name: CR-Diff-05-quotient-3.d
generalfeedback:
In order to solve this problem we will have to use the quotient rule <hint>calc_quotient_rule</hint> as follows:

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
  \frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}\left[{{CT:1}}\right] &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \frac{\left[\frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}[{{CT:2}}]\right]\cdot {{CT:3}} - {{CT:2}}\cdot \left[\frac{d}{d{{CT:0}}}[{{CT:3}}]\right]}{[{{CT:3}}]^2} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \frac{\left[{{CT:4}}\right]\cdot {{CT:3}} - {{CT:2}}\cdot \left[{{CT:5}}\right]}{{CT:6}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \frac{{{CT:7}} - {{CT:8}}}{{CT:6}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \frac{{CT:9}}{{CT:6}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:10}}
 \end{array}\]

on_true.feedback: To differentiate a quotient use the rule \[\frac{d}{dx}\left[\frac{f}{g}\right] = \frac{\frac{df}{dx}g-f\frac{dg}{dx}}{g^2}.\] You cannot get the derivative of a quotient by dividing the derivatives.

You appear to have applied the quotient rule incorrectly.

It is \[\frac{d}{dx}\left[\frac{f}{g}\right] = \frac{\frac{df}{dx}g-f\frac{dg}{dx}}{g^2}.\] It appears that you divided by \(f^2\), not \(g^2\).

You appear to have applied the quotient rule incorrectly.

It is \[\frac{d}{dx}\left[\frac{f}{g}\right] = \frac{\frac{df}{dx}g-f\frac{dg}{dx}}{g^2}.\] You used \[\frac{\frac{df}{dx}g-f\frac{dg}{dx}}{g}.\]

You appear to have applied the quotient rule incorrectly.

It is \[\frac{d}{dx}\left[\frac{f}{g}\right] = \frac{\frac{df}{dx}g-f\frac{dg}{dx}}{g^2}.\] You used \[\frac{\frac{df}{dx}g+f\frac{dg}{dx}}{g^2}.\]
